nodes.summary: Let $h \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible reciprocal polynomial of degree $2k$ such that $h \ne g(x^2)$ for every $g \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$. Then there is exactly one $h_e \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly one $h_o \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly one natural number $\ell$ such that $h_e$ and $h_o$ are reciprocal, $\ell$ is odd and positive, $\deg h_e = k$, $\deg h_o = \max(k - \ell, 0)$,…
nodes.title: Even–odd decomposition of a reciprocal polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible reciprocal $0,1$-polynomial of degree $2m$ such that $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible. Then there is exactly one $f_e \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly one $f_o \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly one natural number $\ell$ such that $f_e$ and $f_o$ are reciprocal $0,1$-polynomials, $\ell$ is odd and positive, $\deg f_e = m$,…
nodes.title: Even–odd decomposition of a reciprocal 0,1-polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic $0,1$-polynomial with fewer than $15$ nonzero coefficients. Then $f(x^{2^n})$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Irreducibility under repeated squaring of the variable

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is non-cyclotomic if and only if $f \ne \Phi_n$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\Phi_n$ denotes the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial.
nodes.title: Characterization of non-cyclotomic polynomials

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is *non-cyclotomic* if $f \ne \Phi_n$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\Phi_n$ denotes the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial.
nodes.title: Non-cyclotomic polynomial

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $d$ (with $d = 0$ for the zero polynomial) is reciprocal if and only if its reversal $x^d f(1/x)$ equals $f$.
nodes.title: Characterization of reciprocal polynomials

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_d x^d$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $d$ (with $d = 0$ for the zero polynomial) is *reciprocal* (palindromic) if it equals its reversal $x^d f(1/x)$, that is, if $a_i = a_{d-i}$ for all $0 \le i \le d$.
nodes.title: Reciprocal polynomial

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is a $0,1$-polynomial if and only if, for every $n \ge 0$, the coefficient of $x^n$ in $f$ is $0$ or $1$.
nodes.title: Characterization of 0,1-polynomials

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is a *$0,1$-polynomial* if every coefficient of $f$ is $0$ or $1$.
nodes.title: 0,1-polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic $0,1$-polynomial of degree $2m$ such that $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible. Let $f_e, f_o \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and let $\ell$ be a positive odd integer with $f(x) = f_e(x^2) + x^\ell f_o(x^2)$, $\deg f_e = m$ and $\deg f_o = \max(m - \ell, 0)$, where the degree of the zero polynomial is taken to be $0$. Then the coefficient of $x^e$ in $f$ is $0$ for…
nodes.title: Position of the first odd exponent

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, with every coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant term $f(0) = 1$. If $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, then $f(x^2) \equiv f(x)\,f(-x) \pmod 4$ as polynomials, that is, the two polynomials have the same image in $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})[x]$.
nodes.title: Square compositions of $0,1$-polynomials modulo $4$

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and of positive degree, with every coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant term $f(0) = 1$. Then $f(x^4)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ if and only if $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
nodes.title: Reducibility of $f(x^4)$ and $f(x^2)$ for $0,1$-polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and let $r \ge 2$ be an integer. Then $f(x^r)$ is reducible if and only if either $f(x^p)$ is reducible for some prime $p$ dividing $r$, or $4$ divides $r$ and $f(x^4)$ is reducible. Here reducible means not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
nodes.title: Capelli's theorem for $f(x^r)$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
